title: The chart verbs print the drain's failure line and exit non-zero
intention: skills/chart/live.py's learn and counsel print each failed drain entry's own stderr line (no second rendering) and, after still serving, exit with a non-zero result code when any pending verdict failed to deposit, so a caller sees the failure in the exit status as well as on stderr.
why: Akien 2026-10-10, verbatim (idea 2026-10-10-so-you-re-running-builder-is-running): "we need to make the queue record stderr. and the result code for heavens sake. and we preapproved all these things thru PROVED". Measured 2026-10-10: ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/verdict-deposits.jsonl holds exactly one line for verdict-20260815T141125-dd35ea1c8f7b, {'kind': 'enqueued', 'at': '2026-09-18T12:56:35', 'ticket': 'b577a9f486dd'}, and nothing else, although every drain since has refused it (VerdictRefused: verdicts[0..2].discriminating_observation must be a non-empty string); the only trace is a stderr print in skills/chart/live.py _drain_before_serving, and the tester on 2026-10-08 could only bound the failure count, not measure it.
traces_to: Law 7 (the deposit ledger is the record of truth for owed deposits and keeps no failure); Law 3 (the failure count is unmeasurable from the record today).
how: skills/chart/live.py only: _drain_before_serving prints entry['stderr'] when present (fallback: today's format, for a codemother that predates 637d206be821) and returns the drained list; add DRAIN_FAILED_EXIT = 3. _counsel and _learn: compute failed = any('failed' in e for e in drained); do everything they do today (serve, print JSON); then return DRAIN_FAILED_EXIT if failed else 0. A refused learn still returns 1 (its own failure outranks a drain failure). Module docstring names exit 3. Charter through the artifact door: public_interface names the exit codes 0/1/3.
falsifier: skills/chart/proofs/test_the_verbs_exit_nonzero_on_a_failed_drain.py under PROVES {'4818f7f37e1e': {'1','2','3'}}, monkeypatching live._ask_codemother (the one bus seam) and live.counsel/_embed/dial: (1) learn with a drain reply carrying one failed entry with stderr 'X' prints exactly 'X' on stderr, still prints its JSON on stdout, and returns 3; (2) counsel likewise returns 3 with its JSON served; (3) with no failed entry both return 0, and a refused deposit returns 1. Hollow: returning 0 unconditionally reds 1 and 2; re-rendering the line reds 1.
watchme: none, because the exit code's consumers are the /chart and /sail skills' own runs (skills/chart/SKILL.md :167, skills/sail/SKILL.md :227), where a non-zero exit is read by CC on the spot

decisions.text: Exit 3, not 1: 1 already means usage or this verb's own refusal; 3 means 'served, but an owed deposit failed'. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09.
Serve first, then exit non-zero: the drain's Law 7 story says the verb still serves. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09.

Edit skills/chart/live.py: add DRAIN_FAILED_EXIT = 3 beside _SENDER; in _drain_before_serving print entry['stderr'] if the failed entry carries it, else today's 'DEPOSIT FAILED — %s STANDS PENDING on the ledger: %s' format; in _counsel and _learn compute failed = any('failed' in e for e in drained) after the drain, serve exactly as today, and return DRAIN_FAILED_EXIT if failed else 0 (the refused-deposit return 1 is untouched and comes first); the module docstring's exit line names 3. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09.

The proof follows the already-written file skills/chart/proofs/test_the_verbs_exit_nonzero_on_a_failed_drain.py (PROVES dict, one function per tooth, main() prints '  green <name>' / '  RED   <name> — ...' and 'N passed, M failed out of K'); it exists red-first at BUILDME. Scenarios: one failed entry carrying stderr (teeth 1, 2); [] and one landed entry (tooth 3, exit 0); refused deposit with [] and with the failed entry (tooth 3, exit 1).
